newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives to set new environmental charges.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives to set new environmental charges.

text.p: Britain's Conservative party will introduce new environmental charges but this would not lead to higher taxes, Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday.

Clarke, launching the ruling party's environmental manifesto ahead of the May 1 election, told a news conference: "As sensible opportunties arose, and after close consultation with those affected, Conservatives will introduce further environmental charges on resourse use and pollution.

"But we will seek to offset such charges by comparable cuts in taxes elsewhere. We will consult on a range of possible economic instruments with environmental benefits, with a view to introducing in the first instance a form of water-pollution charges offset by tax reductions elsewhere."
In a statement issued at the news conference, Prime Minister John Major said the manifesto reflected his party's commitment to substantial, long-term policies on the environment.
"The government I lead has been the greenest that Britain has ever had," Major said.
